To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) university students share generally comparable views on motivations and obstacles to entrepreneurship, with some interesting cultural differences, (b) cultural and social dimensions are only a small portion in explaining entrepreneurial intentions, and (c) psychological self‐efficiency is a significant predictor of entrepreneurial intentions in all three cultural contexts.
entrepreneurial intentions are predicted by a model that includes both cultural and social factors, as well as psychological self-efficacy.
The entrepreneurial intentions of university student entrepreneurs in the USA, in Spain, and in China, are similar.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between cultural, social, psychological, and entrepreneurial factors in the context of entrepreneurship education.
the role of entrepreneurial intentions in explaining entrepreneurial behaviour.
the role of culture in entrepreneurial intentions and how it affects students’ entrepreneurial intentions in different cultural environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the study has provided a strong evidence that entrepreneurial intention of university students is affected by cultural and psychological factors, and that this relationship is mediated through the role of social factors.
the results of this research have shown that the entrepreneurial intentions of university student entrepreneurs are influenced by a variety of factors.
the entrepreneurial intentions are not the same in all the three countries, and this difference is due to the different cultural and social environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the paper is a cross-cultural study of entrepreneurial intentions of university graduates.
the study provides an understanding of the entrepreneurial process in terms of the entrepreneurial intentions of the students.
entrepreneurial intentions are a function of the interaction of cultural, social and psychological variables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between cultural values and entrepreneurial intentions is not straightforward.
the entrepreneurial intention model can be applied to university students from different cultural backgrounds.
entrepreneurship education can be more effective if it takes into account the students’ cultural and social contexts.
